poc_summary: Objective: prove Dedicated pool can meet BlueHarbors latency SLOs for trading desk assistant and large-scale embeddings with transparent unit economics.
Initial reservation: 12 x H100 equivalent (customer asked for H100 spec; Redwood to map to available instance types).
Targets: chat route p95 <= 200ms at sustained 60 RPS (avg response 45 tokens), p99 <= 400ms; embeddings throughput >= 10k embeddings/min with 95% success under steady state.
Success gates: throughput headroom >= 25% over target, error rate < 0.01% during soak, no persistent kernel OOMs, KV cache hit >= 85% in warm run.
Test matrix: 12h ramp to 60 RPS, 48h steady soak, three 15-minute surge events at 2x load, cold-cold restart test (kill service, warm-up measurements), quantized vs fp16 comparison for cost/perf.
Representative prompts: trading-chat (short turn, strict latency), compliance summarize (2-3k token context), reranking pairs (5 candidates), embeddings for batch document ingest.

Deliverables: Redwood console perf dashboard link, CSV/JTL traces, per-model latency histograms, GPU-level utilization and CPE counters, recommended reserved GPU count and burst plan, SLA draft comments.

Routing policy note: BlueHarbor requires EU data residency for EU client traffic; primary Dedicated pool in eu-west for EU routes, us-east for NA. Cross-region fallback only for non-production traffic.
technical_notes: Capacity calc: estimated tokens/request = 55 -> at 60 RPS tokens/sec ~3300; conservative sustained tokens/sec target 4k to include overhead. 12x H100 expected nominal tokens/sec ~18k (theoretical) but we must measure effective throughput given batching inefficiencies and long-contexts.
Batching experiments: target batch sizes 4, 12, 24; measure latency impact vs tokens/sec gains. Evaluate dynamic batching window tuning in Redwood runtime.
KV cache scenarios: warm-cache (simulated high reuse) vs cold-cache (cache miss rates 0-100%); ensure p95 tails are instrumented separately for cache_hit/cold paths.

Soak specifics: 48 hours steady-state chosen (customer prefers 48 over 72 due to calendar), telemetry at 1s resolution for latency percentiles, GPU metrics exported to Grafana for kernel stalls and memory headroom.
Failure modes to capture: long-context kernel stalls, preemption/eviction events on shared infra, slow quantized kernels causing p99 spikes, autoscale latency during surge events.

SLA negotiation items: define per-route latency SLOs, maintenance window policy, credits calculation (linear or tiered), rollback plan when kernel upgrades cause regressions, notification SLAs for incidents.
Commercial preference: fixed monthly reserved fee + lower per-token overage; request option for quarterly reassessment of reserved size based on observed utilization.
